subject: Private connectivity eligibility — FinLytics post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: amir.patel@finlytics.com, psingh@finlytics.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-22T14:12:00Z
Subject: Private connectivity eligibility — quick recap + asks

Hi Amir & Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate you walking us through FinLytics' deployment constraints. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can map a precise connectivity recommendation: 

1) Summary of FinLytics needs (as discussed):
- Production inference for customer-facing analytics (low-100s TPS peak).
- Data residency: US-only.
- Primary preference: Private connectivity (private VPC endpoint or on‑prem) for egress and request traffic.
- Must have either customer-managed outbound IPs or a fixed set of Redwood-managed egress IPs that can be allowlisted.

2) What we need from you to finalize eligibility: 
- Confirm whether you can accept AWS PrivateLink (PrivateLink endpoints) or prefer VPC peering (we covered tradeoffs: PrivateLink = no route propagation, VPC peering = direct routing).
- Do you have a customer NAT / egress device that will originate outbound traffic, or do you want Redwood to provide fixed egress IPs?
- Any on‑prem VPN termination requirements (IPsec tunnels) and the target ASN / public IPs for your edge?

3) Attachments
- MAP-FinLytics-v2.pdf — mutual action plan (draft)
- finlytics-network-sketch.png — rough diagram from today

Next step: if you can send the specific answers above (or confirm in a 15‑minute follow-up), we’ll produce an eligibility note with recommended path (PrivateLink vs peering) and a minimal allowlist snippet for your network team.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@finlytics.com>

Date: 2026-08-22T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Private connectivity eligibility — quick recap + asks

Laura — thanks for the summary. A few quick answers below: 

- Private connectivity: we prefer PrivateLink (AWS) because our networking team wants to avoid route propagation into our prod VPCs; peering is acceptable if PrivateLink is not supported for a given region.
- Egress IPs: ideally Redwood provides a fixed egress IP block we can allowlist. Our current stance is no customer NAT; we want to maintain control on our side for incoming access only.
- On‑prem VPN: we may need an IPsec tunnel for an eventual hybrid deployment; I don't have termination IPs yet — will loop in networkops to provide specifics.

Looping in networkops (networkops@finlytics.com) to provide CIDRs and whether they can accept an external fixed IP allowlist.

Regards,

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: amir.patel@finlytics.com, psingh@finlytics.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T02:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Private connectivity eligibility — quick recap + asks

Amir / Priya — thanks for the quick responses. A few notes from the infra/solutions side to make the allowlist and eligibility more concrete: 

1) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering — what we can offer: 
- AWS PrivateLink (recommended for your preference): we publish an interface endpoint in our account and you create a VPC endpoint in your account. Traffic never traverses the public internet; no route table changes required beyond the endpoint.
- VPC Peering: works cross-account and allows direct routing, but you’ll need route propagation rules and peering acceptance.

2) Egress / Allowlist options: 
- Redwood-managed fixed egress: we can run egress through a fixed set of NAT endpoints we control, and provide a short list of stable IPv4 /24s to allowlist. Example blocks we typically reserve (subject to final provisioning): 34.203.12.0/24, 34.203.13.0/24.
- Customer-managed egress: if you prefer to manage NAT on your side, traffic will originate from your NAT IPs and you won’t need to allowlist Redwood egress.

3) Minimal allowlist snippet for PrivateLink + Redwood egress (example to start conversation):
- 34.203.12.45 (TCP 443 to Redwood interface endpoints)
- 34.203.13.0/24 (optional for monitoring/backoff callbacks)

4) On‑prem VPN / hybrid: we support IPsec termination and can accept customer VPN tunnels; we’ll need the public IP and shared secret to pre-configure the tunnel.

Next steps from our side: I’ll produce a short eligibility note and a one‑page networking checklist (PrivateLink vs peering tradeoffs, required security controls, and the exact allowlist lines) — target EOD tomorrow. If you prefer, we can also schedule a 30‑minute call with your networkops to walk the checklist.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
